newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed little changed on Wednesday, losing most of their earlier gains during a wave of profit-taking in the afternoon.

"We're already discounting the possibility that rates outside Spain will soon start to pick up," a dealer in London said. He expected the 10-year spread over Bunds to narrow and long term interest rates to remain stable round seven percent.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was trading at around 117 basis points. It hit a record low at 104 bps on Monday.
Trading volume was low, as dealers were already looking ahead to the Christmas holidays.
The market shrugged off third quarter GDP which rose 2.2 percent year-on-year, a little more healthy than expected, and also ignored the remarks of Treasury chief Jaime Caruana.

Caruana said the dowtrend in long-term interest rates was not over yet, and the EMU convergence process would continue. Yesterday central bank governor Luis Angel Rojo said long-term rates were close to their bottom.
Foreign markets were also setting the pace for Spanish bonds which tended to copy Italian Btps, which in turn were running out of steam during the day.
